message.content:
On a stormy night, the lighthouse at Blackmoor Point flickered its warning beam into the dark sea. Thomas Grant, the lighthouse keeper, had been alone for weeks, tending to the old light and keeping the logs. The wind howled like a lost soul, and the waves crashed against the rocks with a fury that made even the most seasoned sailors shudder.

As Thomas made his rounds, he noticed something unusual—a bottle, half-buried in the sand near the base of the cliff. Curious, he dug it out and uncorked it with a trembling hand. Inside was a crumpled piece of paper, soaked with saltwater. He wiped it clean and read the message:

*"Dear Keeper, I am lost at sea. My ship was wrecked near these rocks. I have no idea where I am, but I pray you can help me. I am not alone. Please, someone, hear me."*

Thomas’s heart raced. He had heard stories of sailors in distress, but never one so close. He lit the lamp and called for help, sending a distress signal with the light. He also wrote a reply, promising to keep the message safe and to do everything in his power to find the missing sailor.
